name: Sudan
summary_text: Sudan is a place trans visitors should avoid entirely. Article 152 of the Penal Code criminalises gender nonconformity directly; sodomy carries life imprisonment (capital/corporal punishment removed in 2020 reforms); and Cairo 52 documents state violence against LGBTQIA+ people including extrajudicial killings. Since April 2023 the country has been in a catastrophic civil war (SAF vs RSF) with documented mass atrocities — the conflict intensifies every risk and eliminates any recourse. There is no LGR and no community infrastructure. For a visitor: statutory criminalisation of gender nonconformity plus one of the world's worst active conflicts.

sources.title: Sudan | Cairo 52 Legal Research Institute
sources.claim_summary: Cairo 52 country review of Sudan: Article 152 of the penal code criminalises gender nonconformity ('indecent' clothing - 40 lashes or a fine); documented state violence against LGBTQIA+ people including extrajudicial killings; gender-affirming healthcare constrained and no legal recognition; the ongoing conflict intensifies challenges; state reliance on Sunni fatwas obstructs transition.

Human Dignity Trust country profile: Sudan criminalises same-sex sexual activity between men and between women, with sentences including a maximum of life imprisonment (and historically the death penalty for a third offence). (Only the opening was retrievable at fetch time.)

US State Department 2010 Human Rights Report for Sudan: documents the Bashir regime's abuses - extrajudicial killings, torture, Darfur conflict, and the LGBT section noting criminalisation under Article 148 with flogging and death penalty provisions.

Berkouwer, Sultan & Yehia (2014): 'Homosexuality in Sudan and Egypt: Stories of the Struggle for Survival' - by a Harvard research fellow with activists of Bedayaa (the LGBTQI organisation for the Nile Valley); explores daily struggles, discrimination and violence rooted in societal gender and sexual norms, and whether post-Arab-Spring change will transform circumstances.

sources.title: Rainbow Sudan | Sudan's Magazine
sources.claim_summary: Rainbow Sudan: 'Sudan's Magazine' - LGBTI rights in Sudan: history and analysis, organisation profile, and posts on regional LGBTI news and ancient-Egyptian sexuality - a Sudanese LGBTI community resource.

sources.title: Sudan drops death penalty for homosexuality
sources.claim_summary: Erasing 76 Crimes (July 2020): Sudan dropped the death penalty for homosexuality - the Sovereign Council also eliminated 100 lashes, leaving up to 5 years for a first offence, 7 for a second, life for a third; Bedayaa hailed the reforms as 'a great step toward reforming the justice system' while Article 148 remains in force; only six nations then retained the death penalty for gay sex.
